messages:
maya: Quick question — where's the best dashboard for GPU SM% and KV cache hit on prod serving clusters? Seeing a throughput dip on a few models and want to correlate.

liam: Use the Grafana GPU overview -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/gpu-overview/cluster-gpu-overview?orgId=1&var-cluster=prod : panels for SM% (panel: GPU SM Utilization), Memory (GPU memory used / total), and KV cache (panel: KV cache hit rate). Also check per-model route breakdown.

maya: sweet, thanks. Any PromQL I can paste into Explore for a quick check on KV hit ratio and SM%? Not on my laptop for the dashboard now.

liam: PromQL snippets:
- KV cache hit ratio (5m):
  sum(rate(redwood_kvcache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_kvcache_requests_total[5m]))
- GPU SM% (per GPU, 5m avg):
  avg by (instance, pod) (rate(nvidia_gpu_sm_utilization_seconds_total[5m])) * 100
- GPU memory used pct:
  (avg by (instance,pod) (nvidia_gpu_memory_used_bytes) / avg by (instance,pod) (nvidia_gpu_memory_total_bytes)) * 100
- Avg batch size (per route):
  avg_over_time(redwood_infer_batch_size{route=~"/model-.*"}[5m])

sasha: FYI deploy-bot shows a canary rollback in serving yesterday at 16:10 UTC — might explain weirdness on model-x. @deploy-bot can you paste the release id?

deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.14-rc3 -> canary rolled back at 2026-03-14T16:10:23Z due to multiple latency alerts. See runbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runbooks/serving-rollbacks

ethan: When you check SM%, watch for sustained >90% for more than 2 minutes — that's usually contention. If SM% is high and batch size is low, requests are starving and kernel utilization is inefficient.

maya: Got it. I just ran the KV query in Explore — hit ratio dropped from ~0.82 to ~0.28 around the time of the rollback. Memory usage didn't spike, SM% increased across 3 pods.

liam: Looks like the rollback changed model variant to fp16-quantized? That can change KV cache keying if model addresses changed. Check /api/route-config for model-x route to confirm variant.

sasha: Can you grab logs from those pods + a trace? kubectl command:
  kubectl -n serving logs <pod-name> -c runtime --since=30m | grep -i "kvcache" -A3 -B1
And for traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/search?service=serving&trace=*

maya: Will do. Also, can we tune the KV cache alert? Current alert fires when hit_ratio < 0.6 for 10m — it's noisy during rollouts. Suggest 0.4 for rollout windows and add label to suppress for canary-rollbacks.

ethan: Agree on making alert smarter. Proposal:
- severity: page if hit_ratio < 0.25 for 10m
- severity: ticket if 0.25 <= hit_ratio < 0.5 for 30m
- add annotation: if rollout_label=canary then extend window to 30m

liam: I'll open an alert PR in monitoring repo and ping oncall. ETA a couple hours.

maya: Thanks all — I'll attach the pod logs + a sample trace here once I have them.

sasha: :thumbsup: If you need help correlating model variants -> I/O shapes -> KV keys, ping me and I'll pull the deploy manifests.

maya: Uploaded logs and trace snippets. Short summary: rollback coincides with KV key namespace change, hit rate drop, higher SM% and lower throughput. Filing a follow-up to ensure variant deploys keep KV namespace stable.

ethan: Solid. Once alert PR is up, @oncall-sre please watch next rollout and confirm behavior. I'll also add a grafana panel to visualize batch size vs SM% for quick triage.

liam: PR: https://git.redwood.internal/monitoring/pulls/248 — sets new thresholds and rollout label handling. Requesting reviews from @ethan and @oncall-sre.

maya: Awesome, closing loop. Thanks everyone.
